222	title: Keys and typing
223	description: How Frame Job's single-letter keys share the keyboard with text fields, what gives the keys back to the editor, and what Esc leaves.
224	---
225	
226	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
227	
228	Frame Job plays on <kbd>Space</kbd> and trims on <kbd>W</kbd>, so a letter means one thing on the timeline and another in a text field. The rule is short: the keys belong to the editor unless you're typing or a sheet is open.
229	
230	<AtAGlance
231	  keys={['Space', '↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
232	  where={['The editor window', 'The Preview Window']}
233	/>
234	
235	This page explains how the keys are shared. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) has the full list.
236	
237	## Single-letter keys
238	
239	These keys need no modifier and act on the editor window. They also work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).
240	
241	| Key | What it does |
242	| --- | --- |
243	| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play or pause |
244	| <kbd>J</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> <kbd>L</kbd> | Play in reverse, pause, play forward |
245	| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Back or forward one frame, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
246	| <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Previous or next edit point |
247	| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | Start or end of the project |
248	| <kbd>,</kbd> <kbd>.</kbd> | Nudge the selected clips one frame earlier or later, ten with <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
249	| <kbd>I</kbd> <kbd>O</kbd> | Set In, Set Out |
250	| <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> | Trim the start or end to the playhead |
251	| <kbd>M</kbd> | Add Marker |
252	| <kbd>T</kbd> | Add a text clip at the playhead |
253	| <kbd>C</kbd> | Crop mode on or off |
254	| <kbd>Z</kbd> | Region mode for [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) |
255	| <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> | Fit Timeline |
256	| <kbd>N</kbd> | Snapping on or off |
257	| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Deselect the selected action |
258	
259	<kbd>⇧</kbd> and Caps Lock still count as no modifier, so Caps Lock doesn't stop these keys. <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⌃</kbd> always make it a different key.
260	
261	The single-letter keys never fire while you're typing. While a sheet is open none of them works, in either window, so the project can't change underneath the sheet. In the Preview Window they also do nothing while a field in the editor window is still being typed in.
262	
263	Some menu items have a single-letter key the menu doesn't show. [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/) gives those too.
264	
265	### When the focus changes a key
266	
267	A few places claim keys for themselves while they hold the focus:
268	
269	| Where the focus is | What changes |
270	| --- | --- |
271	| The preview canvas | Hold <kbd>Space</kbd> and drag to pan a zoomed canvas. A tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays and pauses. |
272	| The Transcript tab's text | The arrow keys select words. See [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/). |
273	| A selected point on a [curve](/color/curves/) | The arrow keys move the point, <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes it and <kbd>⎋</kbd> deselects it. |
274	| A button, with macOS Full Keyboard Access on | <kbd>Space</kbd> presses the button. |
275	
276	Everywhere else in the window, <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses.
277	
278	## Menu shortcuts
279	
280	Every shortcut with <kbd>⌘</kbd> belongs to a menu item, so it does exactly what the item does. While the item is greyed out, the shortcut does nothing. That includes every editor command while a sheet is open.
281	
282	## Start and finish typing
283	
284	A field takes the keys only when you click in it, or choose a command that opens one for typing, such as **Clip ▸ Rename…** or **View ▸ Assistant**. Nothing else moves the keyboard into a field, so you won't type into one by accident.
285	
286	Any of these applies what you typed and gives the keys back, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away:
287	
288	| Do this | Where it works |
289	| --- | --- |
290	| Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | A one-line field. Multi-line fields have [their own rule](#multi-line-fields). |
291	| Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Any text, including the Assistant's message field |
292	| Click outside the field | Anywhere in the window. The click still does what it would have done, after the field lets go. |
293	
294	<kbd>Tab</kbd> doesn't step through fields. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, it does, and walks to the next control instead.
295	
296	A click on the title bar doesn't end your typing. Neither does a click on the field's own margins or on a text view's scroller, because they count as part of the field. A click on a field's [quick-pick chevron](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick) applies what you typed, then opens its menu.
297	
298	While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> and <kbd>Tab</kbd> belong to it.
299	
300	## Delete keys while you type
301	
302	These four keys act on the timeline when you're not typing. In a text field their menu items switch off, so the keys keep their usual text meaning and a slip of the finger can't delete a clip.
303	
304	| Key | On the timeline |
305	| --- | --- |
306	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> | **Delete** |
307	| <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | **Ripple Delete** |
308	| <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> | **Open Nest** |
309	| <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> | **Close Nest** |
310	
311	## Multi-line fields
312	
313	Four places take more than one line: the Text tab's **Content**, a graphic's multi-line text setting, the Assistant's message field and text you're [editing on the canvas](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/).
314	
315	| Key | What it does |
316	| --- | --- |
317	| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Applies the text. In the Assistant's message field it sends the message, and beeps if the Assistant is busy. |
318	| <kbd>↩</kbd> with any of <kbd>⇧</kbd>, <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌃</kbd> | Starts a new line |
319	
320	On the canvas, <kbd>⎋</kbd> stops editing. If the text changed, Frame Job asks whether to **Apply**, **Revert** or **Cancel**.
321	
322	While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> belongs to it.
323	
324	## Keys in a sheet
325	
326	In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the main button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> presses **Cancel**. The [single-letter keys](#single-letter-keys) stay off until the sheet closes.
327	
328	## What Esc leaves
329	
330	<kbd>⎋</kbd> backs out of whatever is under way.
331	
332	| What's under way | What <kbd>⎋</kbd> does |
333	| --- | --- |
334	| A canvas drag: move, scale, rotate, crop, a line's endpoint or an obscure region | Puts everything back as it was before you pressed, with no undo step |
335	| Crop mode | Leaves it, as <kbd>↩</kbd> does, while the preview canvas holds the focus. <kbd>C</kbd> leaves it from anywhere. |
336	| Region mode, from <kbd>Z</kbd> or the Obscure section's **Place on Canvas** | Leaves it |
337	| The key-colour or qualifier eyedropper | Cancels it |
338	| A selected curve point in the Color tab | Deselects it |
339	| A selected action | Deselects it, so the Clip tab shows the clip's own values again |
340	| Typing in a number field | Throws the typing away |
341	| A rename field on the timeline | Closes it and keeps the old name |
342	| A selection in the Transcript tab | Clears it |
343	
344	Region mode also ends by itself when the selection stops being the clip it started for, or the playhead leaves that clip.
345	
346	A canvas tool that waits for your click or drag shows a crosshair and a hint on the canvas, and only one can wait at a time. The hint says what to do:
347	
348	- "Click to pick the key color · Esc to cancel"
349	- "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel"
350	- "Drag a rectangle to zoom to it · ⇧ fills · Esc to cancel"
351	- "Drag a rectangle to obscure · Esc to cancel"
352	
353	## Related
354

356	- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)
357	- [Gestures with no menu item](/reference/gestures/)

359	title: Undo and saving
360	description: What one undo step is, how the Edit menu names it, what makes no step, and how Autosave keeps your work.
361	---
362	
363	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
364	
365	Every change to a project is a step you can take back. Once a project has been saved, Frame Job also writes your work to disk as you go, so you can try things without worrying about losing it.
366	
367	<AtAGlance
368	  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
369	  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
370	  tools={['undo', 'redo']}
371	/>
372	
373	## Undo and redo
374	
375	**Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) and **Edit ▸ Redo** (<kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>) walk back and forward one step at a time.
376	
377	A new edit clears the redo history, so anything you undid and didn't redo is gone. Each project keeps its last 32 steps.
378	
379	## What counts as one step
380	
381	One step is one thing you did, however many clips it touched.
382	
383	| What you did | How much it counts for |
384	| --- | --- |
385	| A menu command or key | One step, even when it changes many clips. Ripple Delete over a range, Un-nest of several nests, Detach Audio on a selection and a Remove Silences pass are each one. |
386	| A gesture | One step from mouse-down to mouse-up, however long the drag lasts: a move, trim, rate stretch, slip, roll or duplicate-drag. |
387	| An inspector edit | One step for a typed value or a slider press, even with several clips selected. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/). |
388	| A flip of a track's switch, a track rename or a track reorder | Each one is its own step. |
389	
390	## How steps are named
391	
392	The Edit menu names the step it will take back, such as **Undo Move Clips**, and Redo is named the same way. Check the name before you press if you're not sure what you're about to undo.
393	
394	| For | The names you'll see include |
395	| --- | --- |
396	| Clips | Move Clips, Rename Clip, Label Clip |
397	| Tracks | Hide Track, Mute Track, Lock Track, Solo Track, Track Matte, Track Volume, Track Pan, Reset Track Mix, Rename Track, Reorder Track, New Track, Remove Track, Remove Empty Tracks |
398	| Markers | Add Marker, Move Marker, Rename Marker, Chapter Marker, Remove Marker |
399	
400	## What makes no step
401	
402	Anything that doesn't change the project makes no step, so <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> walks straight past it:
403	
404	- Selecting, including a click on a clip that doesn't move it.
405	- Moving the playhead.
406	- Setting the in/out range.
407	- Going into or out of a nest.
408	- An edit Frame Job [wouldn't make](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
409	- An edit that would leave everything as it was.
410	
411	<kbd>⌘Z</kbd> in the Assistant's message field undoes your typing there and never touches the project's steps. Sending the message drops that typing history.
412	
413	## How Autosave keeps your work
414	
415	Once a project has been saved, it autosaves in place as you work, the macOS way. An untitled project has no place of its own on disk until its first Save, so save early. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/) for saving, reverting and browsing earlier versions.
416	
417	The word "edited" in the title bar means changes haven't reached the disk yet. It clears after every silent autosave, and the window's close button never shows a dot.
418	
419	Each save writes the new project beside the old one and swaps it in, so a crash part-way through can't leave you with half a project. See [Crash-safe writes](/projects/save-and-revert/#crash-safe-writes).
420	
421	## With an agent
422	
423	Each agent tool call that edits the project is exactly one step, so one `undo` takes back one call. `undo` and `redo` take no arguments. `undo` reports the name of the step it took back, and it's an error when there's nothing to undo. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).
424	
425	## Related

431	title: When an edit is refused
432	description: How Frame Job tells you it won't make an edit, from the Refused strip in the inspector to a beep with no message, and why nothing changes.
433	---
434	
435	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
436	
437	Frame Job has rules that keep a project sound, such as how far two clips may overlap. When an edit would break one, nothing changes and Frame Job says so. How it says so tells you what happened.
438	
439	<AtAGlance
440	  where={['The foot of the inspector', 'The timeline, for a drop']}
441	/>
442	
443	| What you see | What happened |
444	| --- | --- |
445	| A beep and a **Refused:** line at the foot of the inspector | A rule wouldn't allow the edit |
446	| A clip animates back to the last place it was allowed | The rules wouldn't allow the drop |
447	| A beep and no message | The edit would have changed nothing |
448	| An error alert | Frame Job couldn't use the request at all |
449	
450	Only a drop can still move the clip, to the last allowed place on its way. None of the others changes the project or makes an undo step.
451	
452	## The refusal strip
453	
454	When a rule won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's own sentence at the foot of the inspector, after "Refused: ":
455	
456	> Refused: track 3 is locked, so the gap on it cannot be closed
457	
458	The strip shows up to three lines. Rest the pointer on it to read the whole sentence.
459	
460	It stays until you click it or the project changes, which means an edit, an undo or redo, or going into or out of a nest. Moving the playhead or changing the selection doesn't clear it, so you can look around while you work out what to do.
461	
462	The sentence is exact rather than friendly. It can name clips and tracks by Frame Job's own numbers, which aren't their positions on the timeline, and give lengths in the timeline's smallest units rather than in seconds.
463	
464	Each feature's page lists what can stop it, and [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/) gathers them in one place.
465	
466	A typed Start, Length or end value on an action shows the strip too. Dragging an action's band never does. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
467	
468	## A drop that springs back
469	
470	While you drag, positions the rules don't allow are skipped and the clip waits at the last allowed one. A clip dropped on one of those positions animates back to that place and stays there, as one undo step. If the drag never reached an allowed place, it animates back to where it started and nothing changes. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).
471	
472	## A beep with no message
473	
474	An edit that would change nothing beeps but shows no message, because no rule was broken. A slip does this when the clip is already at the end of its footage, and **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** does it on clips that already have the copied look.
475	
476	## An error alert
477	
478	Now and then Frame Job can't use a request at all, such as a value outside its allowed range. It shows an error alert naming the offending value. You'll rarely meet one, because the inspector's number fields already [hold what you type to their range](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#type-a-value).
479	
480	## With an agent
481	
482	An agent is told the same things in words. An edit a rule won't allow fails with the rule's sentence, and an edit that changes nothing fails saying so. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
483	
484	## Related
485	
486	- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
487	- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)
488	- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)
489	---
490	title: AI features and your own keys
491	description: Which features need nothing, which use an on-device model, which need your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, and what ever leaves your Mac.
492	---
493	
494	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
495	
496	Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. The few features that send your words or audio to a cloud model run on your own API keys, so you decide what's used and you pay the provider directly.
497	
498	<AtAGlance
499	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
500	  keys="⌘,"
501	  where={['Settings ▸ Assistant', 'Settings ▸ Transcription']}
502	  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
503	  needs="Your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, only for the features that send to them."
504	/>
505	
506	## Your own keys
507	
508	There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. There are two keys in all, and each provider bills your account directly.
509	
510	| Key | Turns on | Saved in |
511	| --- | --- | --- |
512	| Anthropic | The Assistant | [Settings ▸ Assistant](/assistant/set-up/) |
513	| AssemblyAI | Cloud captions and Remove Filler Words | [Settings ▸ Transcription](/captions/assemblyai-key/) |
514	
515	Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each Assistant turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The provider's bill is the real figure.
516	
517	With no key set, Settings says "No API key is set." in its ordinary muted colour. That only means there's no key yet, and it isn't an error.
518	
519	## What needs what
520	
521	Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.
522	
523	| What it takes | Features |
524	| --- | --- |
525	| Nothing | Editing, colour, graphics, recording, export and Split at Shot Changes |
526	| An on-device model, with no key and no upload | **Generate Captions** with **On this Mac**, Remove Silences' voice analysis, Enhance Voice and Voice Isolation, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker |
527	| Your AssemblyAI key | The **AssemblyAI** engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** with its **Transcribe** buttons |
528	| Your Anthropic key | The Assistant |
529	
530	Filler removal works only through AssemblyAI. There's no on-device version.
531	
532	Without your Anthropic key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the tab, which says how to add the key.
533	
534	Work you've already paid for keeps working with no key:
535	
536	- **Generate** isn't greyed when every file is already transcribed.
537	- **Remove Filler Words…** stays on while a file it would work on has a current transcript made with filler words.
538	
539	An on-device language that isn't installed yet shows a **Download** row in the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet.
540	
541	## Greyed commands
542	
543	A command that needs a key you haven't set is greyed rather than hidden, and it says which key and where to set it.
544	
545	A greyed menu item's title gains the key's name, as in **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. Rest the pointer on a greyed command or button and it reads:
546	
547	> No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.
548	
549	For the Assistant it's the same sentence with Anthropic and Assistant. The Assistant tab itself reads "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." with an **Open Settings…** button.
550	
551	An agent's tool stops with the same sentence, at the point it would send. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what still works without a key.
552	
553	## Saving a key takes effect at once
554	
555	Saving or removing a key updates open sheets and menu items straight away. An open Generate Captions sheet turns **Generate** back on with the sheet still up, and there's nothing to reopen or relaunch.
556	
557	## What stays on this Mac
558	
559	Editing, analysis, on-device transcription, recording and export all stay on this Mac. Only these reach the network, and each is something you start or can see:
560	
561	| Goes to | What | When |
562	| --- | --- | --- |
563	| AssemblyAI | The audio of the files being transcribed | When you press **Generate** or **Transcribe** with that engine. **Verify** in Settings also makes a small request with your key, with no audio. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/). |
564	| Anthropic | Your Assistant messages, the project's details and the frames it renders | While you use the Assistant. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/). |
565	| GitHub | A request for LiteLLM's published price table, which the cost estimates use, with no key and no project data | At most once a day, from the Assistant's helper |
566	| GitHub | A check of the update feed, and the update itself when you choose to install one | In the [downloaded copy](/getting-started/updates/) only, when you check or if you allowed automatic checks |
567	| macOS's own download | An on-device speech model | When you ask for one |
568	
569	Frame Job has no analytics or telemetry code.
570	
571	## Related
572	
573	- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
574	- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
575	- [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/)
576	- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)
577	---
578	title: Updates
579	description: Check for a newer Frame Job, choose whether it checks by itself, and see which copies update themselves.
580	---
581	
582	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
583	
584	The copy of Frame Job you download keeps itself up to date. It tells you when a new version is ready and installs it when you say so.
585	
586	<AtAGlance
587	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…"
588	  needs="The copy downloaded from the project's GitHub Releases page."
589	/>
590	
591	## Which copy updates itself
592	
593	The copy you download from the project's GitHub Releases page updates itself, with [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org). A copy built from source has no updater: it has no menu item and it never checks.
594	
595	An update is always the whole app. Release notes are on the release's page on GitHub.
596	
597	## Check for updates
598	
599	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…**, directly under **About Frame Job**. It has no shortcut.
600	
601	If a newer Frame Job has been published, a window shows its version. Choose **Install Update** to download it, then **Install and Relaunch** to replace the app and relaunch it. If there's nothing newer, it says you're up to date, and its **Version History** button opens the release's page.
602	
603	The item is greyed while a check is already running. No agent tool checks for updates or installs them.
604	
605	## Automatic checks
606	
607	The second time you open Frame Job, it asks whether to check for updates automatically. If you agree, it checks about once a day while it's open and tells you when an update is ready. It installs one only when you say so, unless you tick **Automatically download and install updates** in that prompt, or the matching box in the update window.
608	
609	Frame Job [remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/) your answer and when it last checked.
610	
611	## Turn automatic checks off
612	
613	There's no Settings control for this. With Frame Job closed, run this in Terminal:
614	
615	```sh
616	defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool NO
617	```
618	
619	**Check for Updates…** still works afterwards.
620	
621	## Signed updates
622	
623	Every update carries an EdDSA signature, and Frame Job won't install one whose signature doesn't match the key built into the app. Only a release published from the project itself can be installed.
624	
625	## Related
626	
627	- [Requirements and install](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/)
628	- [What stays on this Mac](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/#what-stays-on-this-mac)
629	- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)
630
